chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who contracted a mut'ah (temporary) marriage without witnesses. He said: 'There is no objection to the permanent marriage without witnesses between him and God, and the witnesses were instituted in the permanent marriage only for the sake of the child, and if not for that, there would be no objection to it.'
ai.seo_question: Are witnesses required for a valid marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while witnesses are not a strict condition for the intrinsic validity (*sihha*) of permanent marriage (*al-tazwij al-batta*) before God, they are a crucial legal institution (*hukm*) designed to secure lineage (*nasab*) and prevent disputes. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the core contract is consensual, whereas public declaration via witnesses serves a social and evidentiary function rather than constituting a pillar of the contract itself.
